title: Which crypto-condition type does XRPL conditional escrow support, and which fields carry it?
abstract: Sourced guide to the one crypto-condition type XRPL escrow accepts, the Condition and Fulfillment fields, who can finish a conditional escrow and what it costs.
body:
According to the XRPL escrow documentation, the only supported crypto-condition type is PREIMAGE-SHA-256. [1]

An escrow with a condition is created with a corresponding condition and fulfillment. The condition serves as a lock on the funds and will not release them until the correct fulfillment is provided. Anyone can finish such an escrow, but only by supplying the correct fulfillment; when the conditions are met the Escrow object is destroyed and the funds go to the recipient. If no one finishes it before its CancelAfter time, the escrow expires and anyone can cancel it. [1]

According to the XRPL EscrowFinish reference, the Condition field is the previously supplied PREIMAGE-SHA-256 crypto-condition of the escrow, and the Fulfillment field is the PREIMAGE-SHA-256 crypto-condition fulfillment matching the escrow's Condition. An escrow that has a Condition cannot be executed without a matching Fulfillment. A transaction that contains a fulfillment costs 330 drops of XRP plus another 10 drops for every 16 bytes in size of the preimage. [2]

Author interpretation: PREIMAGE-SHA-256 means the condition commits to the SHA-256 hash of a secret, and revealing that secret in EscrowFinish is what unlocks the funds. Anything built on this, such as a key-reveal delivery, should treat the fulfillment as public once the transaction is submitted. Sources accessed 11 November 2026. [1][2]
